name: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
summary: Held that the procedure established by law under Article 21 must be strictly procedural, giving a narrow interpretation of personal liberty.

name: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
summary: Established the Basic Structure Doctrine. Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure.

name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
summary: Expanded Article 21 to include the right to life and personal liberty. Held that procedure must be fair, just, and reasonable.

name: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
summary: Struck down parts of the 42nd Amendment. Reaffirmed the Basic Structure Doctrine and judicial review.

name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
summary: A nine-judge bench unanimously held that the right to privacy is a fundamental right inherent in Article 21.
